anchors.statement: Each atm-bd-console dispatch, hold, marker or section rule must be a single check on snapshot fields that does not depend on the result of any other rule.
anchors.scope: any bead that defines or changes a dispatch, hold, escalation, marker or section rule

pass: Each dispatch rule is one check on snapshot fields: stage is sanity or QA, the bead has a branch, one PR is open, the worktree exists.
fail: QA is dispatched only if sanity passed, and if that check fails the dispatcher then checks CI before deciding whether to retry the stack-top check.

anchors.statement: Every atm-bd-console dispatch, escalation and section rule must be implemented in exactly one module, and the app, the cron mode and bead-queues must call that module rather than contain their own copy of any rule.
anchors.quote: business logic defined clearly in a single place.
anchors.scope: any bead that adds code to render.py, cli.py, app.py or bead-queues

pass: All dispatch and section rules live in dispatch.py and model.py; render.py, cli.py and bead-queues only call them.
fail: bead-queues keeps its own copy of the section rules so it can run without the app installed.

anchors.statement: Running atm-bd-console as the cron job and as the TUI app must produce the same dispatches, messages and state for the same beads and tasks.
anchors.quote: identical behavior when run as cron or tui
anchors.scope: any bead that changes the tick, the app loop or the cron mode

pass: The app loop and --once --headless call the same tick function and a test runs both against one fixture and compares dispatches, messages and state.
fail: The cron mode skips escalation batching to stay fast; only the app batches resends.

anchors.statement: The atm-bd-console dispatcher must not hold or skip a sanity or QA dispatch for any reason that the production atm-bd-orchestration rules do not already use.
anchors.quote: we are working off a set of rules already in production.
anchors.scope: any bead that defines when sanity or QA is dispatched or held

pass: The dispatcher sends sanity or QA when bd ready lists the bead, the branch has one open PR and the worktree exists; nothing else holds it.
fail: QA waits until the PR's CI is green and the layer is the top of the stack.

anchors.scope: any bead that adds a bd read

pass: Each tick reads open beads with bd list -l phase-bh and fetches needed closed ids with one batched bd show.
fail: Each tick runs bd list --all to find closed predecessors.

anchors.statement: atm-bd-console must make no GitHub call on a tick that dispatches nothing.
anchors.quote: I thought there were no gh calls
anchors.scope: any bead that adds a gh or GitHub API call

pass: An idle tick reads only bd and atm; GitHub is called once per sanity or QA dispatch.
fail: Each tick fetches open PRs from GitHub to refresh the dashboard.

anchors.statement: atm-bd-console must refuse to start without `--as` and must print a message explaining what `--as` is.
anchors.quote: I would prefer that bead-dispatch makes --as a mandetory arg w/ good console message if it is not set
anchors.scope: any bead that defines the CLI arguments or the assigning identity

pass: Without --as the CLI exits 3 and prints what --as is and an example command.
fail: Without --as the CLI uses $ATM_IDENTITY as the lead.

anchors.statement: The dashboard must show, for each agent, its total number of assigned tasks and at most 3 of those tasks.
anchors.quote: what i want to see is what tasks agents are assigned. i.e. queue per agent (up to a limit around ~3. if > 3 tasks, I still want to know queue depth).
anchors.scope: any bead that defines the agent blocks

pass: Each agent block shows the agent's queue depth and up to 3 task rows, then '… +N more'.
fail: The dashboard lists only the running task of each agent.

anchors.statement: The dashboard must mark each assigned task whose bead is not part of the current phase's sprints.
anchors.quote: I also want to know if these are not sprint tasks.
anchors.scope: any bead that defines the snapshot rows or the agent blocks

pass: A task whose bead's top epic is not the phase root shows a red marker; a task with no bead shows a yellow marker.
fail: Tasks are listed by agent without any phase check.

anchors.statement: Unresolved problems must be resent to the lead together in one message 10 minutes after the first escalation, and every 10 minutes after that.
anchors.quote: one message per problem, then resent after 10 minutes. if more issues show up, batch them into same 10 minute interval after 1st send.
anchors.scope: any bead that defines escalation or hold messages

pass: Problems at 1m, 2m and 3m are sent at 1m, 2m and 3m, and resent together in one message at 11m.
fail: Each unresolved problem is resent individually every tick until resolved.

anchors.statement: Once the phase root bead is closed, atm-bd-console must not poll, dispatch or send messages, whether it runs as the app or as the cron job.
anchors.quote: app would stop polling and cron would do nothing when phase ended.
anchors.scope: any bead that defines the tick start, the app loop or the cron mode

pass: When the root bead is closed, the app stops ticking and shows closed; the cron run exits 0 after the root check.
fail: When the root closes, the app keeps polling every 60 s and shows no new rows.

anchors.statement: Every dashboard line must fit the terminal width without wrapping, with descriptions truncated to fit.
anchors.quote: for all descriptions, we need to truncate so no line wrap occurs
anchors.scope: any bead that defines dashboard output

pass: Line width is read from the terminal on every redraw and descriptions are truncated with an ellipsis.
fail: Long descriptions wrap onto a second indented line.

anchors.statement: Each dashboard row must contain only an icon, a task id, an age, a tag and a description.
anchors.quote: avoid any text that is not necessary. concise and narrower
anchors.scope: any bead that defines dashboard output

pass: A row is: icon, id, age, tag, description.
fail: Each row also shows the assignee name, bead status and full bead labels.
